result.evidence: The hypothesis describes traffic signal adaptation using reinforcement learning with independent intersection agents and reward functions based on local traffic metrics. The source document discusses Physarum polycephalum's network adaptation through protoplasmic streaming and tube thickness changes based on flow rates. While both systems involve distributed adaptation through local feedback, the mechanisms (reinforcement learning vs. biological protoplasmic streaming), domains (traffic engineering vs. biological organisms), and specific implementation details (reward functions vs. actin-myosin contractions) are fundamentally different. This represents a cross-domain transfer of the general concept of distributed network optimization through local feedback, not a direct composition or paraphrase of the source content.
